bsm_101.text: Joanie Faust says, "It is nothing! It is a fact about your body! It is not a skill, it is not a trade, it is not a CHARACTER. You are a boy who washes plates and got dealt one card and you are about to sell it to a man in a coat."

bsm_102.text: Denny Faust says, "He said I could be somebody."

bsm_103.text: Joanie Faust says, "He said you could be LOOKED AT. Those are different words and he chose the one he chose because he has done this before."

bsm_104.text: Denny Faust says, "At least he came to the house. At least somebody came."

bsm_105.text: Joanie Faust says, "You’re nothing. Do you hear me? Under the one thing, you are nothing, and the world is going to find that out for you and it will not be gentle about the lesson."

bsm_106.text: The porch light hums. It is the only sound in the house for four seconds.

bsm_107.text: Denny Faust says, "Then I’ll find out."

bsm_108.text: Denny takes a coat off the hook. He does not slam anything, which is somehow worse.

bsm_109.text: He walks. The porch light stays on behind him for a long time, because she does not turn it off, because turning it off would be admitting he is not coming back.

bsm_11.text: The Meridian is a roadhouse built into the shell of a truck depot. Two hundred people, one working ceiling fan, and a stage the size of a card table.

bsm_111.text: THE PRINE HOUSE, ABOVE THE BASIN

bsm_112.text: Auggie Prine does not own a studio. Auggie Prine owns a HOUSE, which is different, and which is the entire point of Auggie Prine.

bsm_113.text: The pool is drained and full of cable. The lounge is a set. The kitchen is a green room. Sixteen people live here who are not related to each other and would all say they are.

bsm_114.text: At the centre of it, on a lounger, holding court over a room she has never once needed to raise her voice in, is MARGUERITE SABLE.

bsm_115.text: Marguerite Sable says, "You’re the boy from the roadhouse."

bsm_117.text: Marguerite Sable says, "Not for long, sweetheart. Come sit down before you fall down. Have you eaten anything that wasn’t out of a machine this week?"

bsm_119.text: Marguerite Sable says, "That’s a no. Kestrel, get him a plate."

bsm_12.text: Behind the bar, MAURICE TAM runs the room the way a man runs a boiler he does not fully understand.

bsm_120.text: KESTREL rolls in from the kitchen. She is seventeen and she has a broadcast headset clamped over her ears that she does not take off, has not taken off, and will not take off in this entire picture.

bsm_121.text: Kestrel says, "He can get his own plate. Is this the one Auggie’s been going on about?"

bsm_122.text: Marguerite Sable says, "This is the one."

bsm_123.text: Kestrel says, "He’s been saying "wait till you see it" for three days like a man with a boat."

bsm_124.text: REED HALLORAN comes down the stairs with the specific confidence of a man who has never once been the smartest person in a room and has never once noticed.

bsm_125.text: Reed Halloran says, "Is this him? This is him. Hey. Reed Halloran. I’m the other one."

bsm_127.text: Reed Halloran says, "The other guy in the scene. There’s always two guys. One of them’s the one they came for and one of them’s the one who makes the first one look taller. I’m very good at it."

bsm_128.text: Marguerite Sable says, "Reed’s being modest. Reed can hit a mark in the dark and cry on the count of four."

bsm_129.text: Reed Halloran says, "I can. Watch. One. Two. Three."

bsm_13.text: Out back, in the wash pit, a nineteen-year-old named DENNY FAUST scrapes plates for nine credits an hour.

bsm_130.text: Reed cries. It is instantaneous and completely convincing and he stops just as fast.

bsm_131.text: Reed Halloran says, "Four. See? Every time. It’s a gift and it has cost me two marriages."

bsm_132.text: WILBY CRANE is in the corner with a sound cart, headphones on, adjusting something that does not need adjusting. He does not look up.

bsm_133.text: Wilby Crane says, "Tell him to stand on the tape."

bsm_134.text: Auggie Prine says, "Denny, stand on the tape."

bsm_135.text: Denny stands on a strip of tape on the floor. It is the first mark he has ever hit. He will hit thousands.

bsm_136.text: Auggie Prine says, "Everybody. Come here a minute."

bsm_137.text: Marguerite Sable says, "Auggie, the boy just walked in."

bsm_138.text: Auggie Prine says, "Marguerite, in this house we do not do the thing where everybody finds out one at a time in a corridor over four weeks. We do it once, we do it in daylight, and then it is over and he is a colleague."

bsm_139.text: He turns to Denny, and the enormous kindness of Auggie Prine is that he asks.

bsm_14.text: At the end of the bar, in a coat too good for the room, a big man is watching the kitchen door. This is AUGGIE PRINE.

bsm_140.text: Auggie Prine says, "Is that alright with you?"

bsm_142.text: Sixteen people in a lounge in a rented house look at a nineteen-year-old dishwasher, and the film gives us their faces and not him.

bsm_143.text: Reed Halloran laughs out loud, once, and then apologises, and then laughs again.

bsm_144.text: Marguerite Sable does not laugh. She looks at him for a long moment with something close to pity, because she is thirty-four and she knows exactly what a room full of that face costs.

bsm_145.text: Kestrel takes one hand off her plate and pushes her headset back a quarter inch, which for Kestrel is a standing ovation.

bsm_146.text: Wilby Crane says nothing at all, because Wilby Crane is a sound man and this is not his department.

bsm_147.text: Reed Halloran says, "Okay. Okay! Right. Okay. So... I’m the other one. I want that on the record. I’ve made my peace with it in the last four seconds."

bsm_149.text: Auggie Prine says, "Thank you, everybody. That’s the whole ceremony. We shoot Thursday."

bsm_15.text: Auggie Prine says, "Maurice. The boy carrying the crates."

bsm_150.text: The room goes back to being a room. Somebody puts something on. It takes about forty seconds and then it is genuinely, completely over, which is the single most decent thing that happens to Denny Faust in this entire picture.

bsm_151.text: Marguerite Sable says, "He can’t work under Denny Faust. It sounds like a boy who mows lawns."

bsm_152.text: Auggie Prine says, "He’s not going to work under Denny Faust."

bsm_154.text: Auggie Prine says, "Something with a stop in it. Something the ear catches. Two syllables and a hard letter."

bsm_155.text: Denny is standing on his mark in a stranger’s living room in a house above a dead city, being renamed by people who have known him for eleven minutes, and he does not stop it.

bsm_158.text: Denny Faust says, "Vox. My mother had a hymn book. It was in the hymn book."

bsm_159.text: Marguerite Sable says, "Vox. That’s good. That’s not bad at all. Vox what, though. You need a front half."

bsm_16.text: Maurice Tam says, "That’s Denny. He does the plates. Don’t."

bsm_160.text: Reed Halloran says, "Something churchy. He’s got that face. He’s got a face like a boy who’s about to confess to something."

bsm_162.text: Everyone turns and looks at the seventeen-year-old in the headset, who has not looked up from her plate.

bsm_163.text: Kestrel says, "Deacon Vox. It sounds like a man on a poster. Can I go now."

bsm_164.text: Auggie Prine says, "Nobody move. Say it out loud, all of you. I want to hear it in a room."

bsm_168.text: And there it is, in a rented house, in front of sixteen people, said aloud four times until it stopped being a joke and started being a name.

bsm_171.text: THE PRINE HOUSE, THE LOUNGE SET

bsm_172.text: The first shoot. Three lamps, one camera, a bedsheet on a frame, and more concentration in the room than most governments manage in a year.

bsm_173.text: This is the part nobody outside this house understands. It is a workplace. There are marks on the floor and a schedule on the wall and a man with a clipboard worrying about the lamps.

bsm_176.text: Auggie Prine says, "Scotty, boom’s in frame, come up two inches. Two. Two, Scotty."

bsm_177.text: SCOTTY KELL, nineteen, adores everyone in this room in a way that is going to cost him, and comes up two inches.

bsm_179.text: Auggie Prine says, "Don’t be sorry, be two inches higher. Marguerite, you’re on the couch. Deacon, you come in on the line."

bsm_18.text: Maurice Tam says, "Whatever it is you do. I know what you do. Everybody knows what you do."

bsm_181.text: Auggie Prine says, "Tired. Not sad. Tired is more expensive than sad."

bsm_182.text: Marguerite Sable says, "Tired I can do without acting."

bsm_183.text: Marguerite Sable takes her robe off and hands it to a woman whose entire job is to hold it, and sits down on a couch, and is at work.

bsm_184.text: Marguerite Sable says, "Sweetheart. Look at me a second."

bsm_186.text: Marguerite Sable says, "First one. Everybody’s first one is bad and nobody remembers it. Look at my face, not the lens, not Auggie, not the boom. My face is the whole job."

bsm_188.text: Marguerite Sable says, "And if it doesn’t happen, it doesn’t happen. It happens to everybody, it happened to Reed twice last month..."

bsm_189.text: Reed Halloran says, "It was ONCE, Marguerite, and there was a wasp in the room."

bsm_19.text: Auggie Prine says, "Then you know I do it politely."

bsm_190.text: Marguerite Sable says, "And we go again after lunch and nobody says a word about it. Nobody in this house has ever said a word about it."

bsm_192.text: Deacon Vox walks into frame in a stranger’s living room and says the first line he will ever say on tape.

bsm_193.text: Deacon Vox says, "You left the light on for me."

bsm_194.text: Marguerite Sable says, "I always leave the light on."

bsm_195.text: Deacon Vox says, "The grid’s out three nights a week. That light costs you something."

bsm_196.text: Marguerite Sable says, "Everything costs me something. The light I don’t mind."

bsm_197.text: And then they do the rest of it, and the film stays where it has been the whole scene, which is at the back of the room with the crew.

bsm_198.text: We watch Auggie Prine watch his monitor. We watch the clipboard man stop worrying about the lamps. We watch Scotty Kell’s arms shake holding the pole and not drop it.

bsm_199.text: We watch Wilby Crane, on the cart, take his headphones off, which Wilby Crane does not do, and look at the monitor like a man checking a number he has already checked.

bsm_20.text: Maurice Tam says, "You do it politely and they never come back to the plates. That’s two dishwashers you’ve had off me."

bsm_200.text: Nobody in the room says anything for a long time after Auggie says cut. That is not a compliment. That is a room full of professionals doing arithmetic.

bsm_201.text: Auggie Prine says, "Cut. Print. Wilby, tell me."

bsm_202.text: Wilby Crane says, "I want to go outside for a minute."

bsm_204.text: Wilby Crane goes outside and stands in a drained swimming pool full of cable and does not do anything in particular, because there is nothing in his trade to do about what he has just watched.

bsm_205.text: Reed Halloran says, "That was one take. That was ONE TAKE, Auggie."

bsm_206.text: Auggie Prine says, "I know what it was."

bsm_207.text: Reed Halloran says, "I’ve never done one take. I did nineteen takes of a man opening a door."

bsm_208.text: Auggie Prine says, "You were bad at opening the door, Reed."

bsm_209.text: Reed Halloran says, "I was! I was terrible at it! It’s a hard door!"

bsm_21.text: Auggie Prine turns on his stool so that he is facing the room, which is what he does instead of arguing.

bsm_210.text: Marguerite Sable puts the robe back on and lights something and does not say anything at all, and later she will tell Auggie that in eleven years she has never once been nervous on a couch and she was nervous on that couch.

bsm_211.text: Kestrel says, "It’s going to be huge."

bsm_212.text: Auggie Prine says, "It’s going to be huge."

bsm_213.text: Kestrel says, "No, I mean it’s going to be HUGE. I’m on the feed all night. There’s nothing out there. There is nothing out there but weather and lists."

bsm_216.text: A montage, which is a lie a film tells to skip the boring parts of getting rich.

bsm_217.text: A rented room in the Rust District. A woman at two in the morning, alone, with a set on. She has not moved in forty minutes.

bsm_218.text: A bar in Coldwater where the whole room turns to face the box, and a man who is losing at cards asks for quiet, and the barman does not change the channel even though there are women present, because the women asked him not to.

bsm_219.text: A checkpoint on the East Road where two militia stop arguing about a bribe because the guard-hut set is on and something is happening on it.

bsm_22.text: Auggie Prine says, "Maurice, why does a nineteen-year-old dishwasher get talked about in a bar he isn’t drinking in?"

bsm_220.text: The tape went out on an unlicensed mast on a Tuesday. By Friday it had been recopied four hundred times by people with no equipment and worse ethics.

bsm_221.text: Nobody paid Auggie Prine for a single copy. That was not how it worked. It worked like weather.

bsm_222.text: What Auggie Prine got instead was the next one, financed by everyone in the Basin who wanted to be near it.

bsm_224.text: The Colonel has arrived. THE COLONEL is a soft man in a good coat who has never raised his voice because he has never had to.

bsm_225.text: The Colonel says, "Auggie. I have watched your tape eleven times."

bsm_227.text: The Colonel says, "And I have not watched anything eleven times since the Handoff. I have not watched anything TWICE."

bsm_228.text: Auggie Prine says, "What are you offering, Colonel."

bsm_229.text: The Colonel says, "Six thousand a picture. Tape stock. Two more lamps."

bsm_230.text: Auggie Prine says, "Ten. And I keep the negative."

bsm_231.text: The Colonel says, "Nobody keeps the negative, Auggie, there is no law that says you keep the negative."

bsm_232.text: Auggie Prine says, "There is no law that says anything, which is why the man holding the negative is the man who owns it. Ten."

bsm_233.text: The Colonel says, "Eight. And I want him in every one."

bsm_234.text: Auggie Prine says, "He’s in every one anyway. That wasn’t a concession, that was you describing the weather to me and calling it a deal."

bsm_235.text: The Colonel laughs. It is not a warm sound. Nothing about the Colonel is warm, and everybody in this picture will spend two years politely not noticing.

bsm_236.text: The Colonel says, "I like you, Auggie. You’re the only man in the Basin still pretending this is a craft."

bsm_237.text: Auggie Prine says, "It IS a craft."

bsm_238.text: The Colonel says, "It’s a hole in the world and everybody’s pouring themselves into it. But you make it look like a craft, and I’ll pay for the look."

bsm_24.text: Auggie Prine says, "He does. I have been in this room four times and I have heard about that boy from three different women who do not know each other, and one of them was crying laughing, and one of them was not laughing at all."

bsm_241.text: Deacon Vox has a room now. In it are a bed, a full-length mirror, and eleven hundred credits in a shoebox, which is more money than his mother has ever held at one time.

bsm_242.text: He stands in front of the mirror for a while. He is not vain about it yet. That comes later, and it comes fast, and it is the beginning of everything that goes wrong.

bsm_243.text: Right now he is nineteen and he is looking at himself the way you look at a lottery ticket you have not cashed.

bsm_246.text: Kestrel is in the doorway, headset on, watching him look at himself the way you watch a dog dream.

bsm_247.text: Kestrel says, "You do that every night."

bsm_248.text: Deacon Vox says, "I’ve been here eight days."

bsm_249.text: Kestrel says, "You’ve done it eight times. I’m very observant, it’s my whole personality, I don’t have any others."

bsm_25.text: Maurice Tam says, "It’s a small district."

bsm_250.text: Deacon Vox says, "What are you listening to? You’re always listening to something."

bsm_251.text: Kestrel says, "Everything. All of it. Every channel that’s still up, all night, all at once."

bsm_253.text: Kestrel says, "Because if I take it off it’s quiet, and when it’s quiet I can hear the house, and when I can hear the house I remember I live here on purpose."

bsm_254.text: Deacon Vox says, "Can I ask you something?"

bsm_255.text: Kestrel says, "You’re going to ask if it’s always this easy."

bsm_257.text: Kestrel says, "It’s this easy for about three years. Ask Marguerite what year four is like. Actually don’t, she’ll tell you, and then you’ll have to know it."

bsm_258.text: She rolls off down the hall. Deacon Vox looks at himself in the mirror for a long moment, and then says his own name out loud to see whether it fits yet.

bsm_26.text: Auggie Prine says, "It is a small district and I am a patient man and I would like you to say the thing out loud so that we can both stop performing."

bsm_262.text: A year in. The house is fuller, louder, and better fed. There are now two cameras, which in this business is an empire.

bsm_263.text: BUCK OZAROW is at the table with a catalogue, a calculator, and the doomed patience of a man building a plan out of a world that does not take plans.

bsm_264.text: Buck Ozarow says, "Eleven thousand four hundred. That’s the number."

bsm_265.text: Reed Halloran says, "That’s the number for what?"

bsm_266.text: Buck Ozarow says, "For the shop. Buck’s Audio. Two rooms on the Coldwater strip, a bench, a soldering station, and every speaker in the Basin that still works comes through my door."

bsm_267.text: Reed Halloran says, "Nobody fixes speakers, Buck."

bsm_268.text: Buck Ozarow says, "Everybody NEEDS speakers fixed. Nobody fixes them. Do you understand that those are two halves of the same sentence and the sentence is money?"

bsm_269.text: Marguerite Sable says, "Buck, honey, that’s the smartest thing anyone’s said in this house in eleven months."

bsm_27.text: Maurice Tam wipes a glass that is already clean, which is what a man does when he has decided to say it.

bsm_272.text: Buck Ozarow says, "Why won’t it happen?"

bsm_273.text: Marguerite Sable says, "Because nobody lends to us. Look at me. Look at what I do. I have eleven thousand credits in a coffee tin because no bank in the Basin will hold it."

bsm_274.text: Buck Ozarow says, "The Meridian Mutual takes anybody. It says so on the sign. It says "we take anybody.""

bsm_275.text: Marguerite Sable says, "It means anybody with a job they can say out loud."

bsm_278.text: Buck Ozarow, in his best coat, sitting very straight, across from a clerk with a form and a policy and no particular malice.

bsm_28.text: Maurice Tam says, "He’s built wrong. That’s the polite version and it’s the only version you’re getting from me."

bsm_283.text: the licensing clerk says, "Mister Ozarow, the form has a box and the box has a word in it. I am going to have to ask you to say the word."

bsm_284.text: Buck Ozarow says, "Adult. Adult broadcast. I’m on the tapes."

bsm_285.text: The clerk stops writing. She does not sneer. It is much worse than a sneer. She simply stops writing, and puts the cap back on the pen, which is a decision.

bsm_287.text: Buck Ozarow says, "It’s legal. There isn’t a law about it. There isn’t a law about anything."

bsm_288.text: the licensing clerk says, "It is not a question of legality, Mister Ozarow. It is a question of character. The lending policy requires character."

bsm_289.text: Buck Ozarow says, "I have character. I have eleven thousand credits of character. I have never missed a payment on anything in my life because I have never been ALLOWED to owe anything."

bsm_290.text: the licensing clerk says, "The policy is the policy. I’m sorry."

bsm_291.text: Buck Ozarow says, "No you’re not. You’re not sorry, you’re relieved. There’s a difference and I can hear it, I work in sound."

bsm_292.text: He takes his coat off the back of the chair with enormous dignity and leaves, which is the only thing left to take.

bsm_294.text: THE PRINE HOUSE, THE POOL DECK

bsm_295.text: Auggie Prine holds court in a drained pool. This is where he does his thinking, because it is the only place in the house with no cable in it.

bsm_296.text: Auggie Prine says, "I want to do something and everyone is going to tell me it’s a mistake."

bsm_298.text: Auggie Prine says, "You haven’t heard it."

bsm_299.text: Wilby Crane says, "I’ve worked for you for nine years, Auggie. It’s a mistake and I’ll do it."

bsm_3.text: A held shot on a transmitter mast at dusk, red light blinking, nobody underneath it. It has been blinking without instruction for eleven years. Nobody has ever gone up to ask it why.

bsm_30.text: Maurice Tam says, "Auggie, the boy is nineteen years old and he is the most talked-about thing in East Basin and he does not know it yet, and I would like it very much if that lasted another year."

bsm_300.text: Auggie Prine says, "I want to make one that’s ninety minutes. One story. Same people the whole way through. A beginning that you have to sit through to understand the end."

bsm_301.text: Reed Halloran says, "Who sits still for ninety minutes?"

bsm_302.text: Auggie Prine says, "Everybody used to! Everybody in the world used to! They used to leave the HOUSE to do it, Reed, they used to pay money and sit in the dark with strangers for two hours and nobody thought that was strange!"

bsm_303.text: Reed Halloran says, "And then the world ended."

bsm_304.text: Auggie Prine says, "And then the world ended and we all decided people are only good for four minutes at a time. I don’t accept it. I have never accepted it."

bsm_305.text: Marguerite Sable says, "Auggie. Sweetheart. Tell them the real reason."

bsm_306.text: Auggie Prine says, "That is the real reason."

bsm_307.text: Marguerite Sable says, "Tell them the other real reason."

bsm_308.text: Auggie Prine is quiet for a moment. In the drained pool his voice does that thing that voices do in a drained pool.

bsm_309.text: Auggie Prine says, "Because everybody in the Basin already knows what we sell and everybody in the Basin already gets it for free, and the ONLY thing left to be good at is the ninety minutes around it."

bsm_31.text: Auggie Prine says, "It will not last another year. It was never going to last another year. That is not me, that is arithmetic."

bsm_310.text: Auggie Prine says, "And because in forty years there will be nothing left from now. Nothing. Everything we make gets recopied into mud and everything before us is in a corp vault."

bsm_311.text: Auggie Prine says, "And if there is going to be exactly one thing left that says people were here and they were trying, I would like it to be ninety minutes long and I would like it to be GOOD."

bsm_312.text: Nobody says anything for a while. Kestrel takes her headset off. It is the only time in this picture that she does.

bsm_317.text: A montage of the good years, which is the part everybody remembers and nobody was paying attention during.

bsm_318.text: A new mast on the ridge, paid for in cash, wired by four people who did not know what they were doing and did it anyway.

bsm_319.text: Deacon Vox on a poster on a wall in the Yards, and a queue of people waiting outside a bar to watch a broadcast on a screen the size of a door.

bsm_32.text: Auggie finishes his drink and does not order another, which in this bar is a kind of announcement.

bsm_320.text: Marguerite Sable teaching Kestrel how to hit a mark. Kestrel hitting the mark. Kestrel hitting the mark better than Marguerite Sable.

bsm_321.text: Buck Ozarow in a shirt he bought for himself, carrying a speaker cabinet up the stairs of a house that is not his, whistling.

bsm_322.text: Scotty Kell learning to keep the boom out of frame, mostly, on the eighth try, to genuine applause.

bsm_323.text: Reed Halloran crying on the count of four, in a wide shot, in the rain, for the fourteenth time, without complaint, because it is the job.

bsm_324.text: And Deacon Vox in the middle of it, at twenty-one, with money in a shoebox and a family who chose him and a body that has not failed him once.

bsm_325.text: For about three years, in a rented house above a dead city, a group of people who had been thrown away by everything made the best work of their lives.

bsm_326.text: It is important to say that out loud, because of what happens next, and because everyone who tells this story afterwards leaves this part out.

bsm_328.text: THE BASIN BROADCAST AWARDS, COLDWATER CIVIC HALL

bsm_329.text: An awards night thrown by an industry that legally does not exist, in a hall with a hole in the roof, with trophies made from transmitter parts.

bsm_33.text: Auggie Prine says, "Two dishwashers, you said. Where are they now?"

bsm_330.text: It is, without any irony at all, the happiest night of everybody’s life.

bsm_331.text: Auggie Prine says, "Best Tape. Best Direction. Best Performance, Male. Three."

bsm_332.text: Wilby Crane says, "Four. They gave one to Scotty."

bsm_333.text: Auggie Prine says, "They gave one to SCOTTY?"

bsm_334.text: Wilby Crane says, "Best Boom. They invented it tonight. He’s crying in the corridor."

bsm_336.text: Wilby Crane says, "He’s crying in the corridor."

bsm_337.text: Marguerite Sable comes off the stage holding a trophy welded out of a broken antenna, and she is not entirely present.

bsm_338.text: Marguerite Sable says, "Auggie. Auggie, I have to tell you something and you have to not make a thing of it."

bsm_34.text: Maurice Tam says, "One of them has a house."

bsm_340.text: Marguerite Sable says, "I filed for the boy again. My son. The hearing’s in the spring."

bsm_342.text: Marguerite Sable says, "It’s not wonderful, it’s the fourth time. They ask what I do. Every time they ask what I do and every time I say it and every time I watch them write it down."

bsm_343.text: Auggie Prine says, "So say something else."

bsm_344.text: Marguerite Sable says, "I’m not ashamed of it."

bsm_345.text: Auggie Prine says, "I didn’t say be ashamed of it. I said SAY something else. There is a difference between shame and strategy and one of them gets you your son back."

bsm_346.text: Marguerite Sable says, "Auggie, they have watched the tapes. That is the part nobody says. Somebody in that building has sat down and watched me work in order to decide whether I am fit, and then gone home to his family."

bsm_348.text: Marguerite Sable says, "He’s eleven. He lives in an arcology creche in a building I am not allowed into. He has a number. My son has a NUMBER, Auggie."

bsm_349.text: She stops. She puts the trophy down on a table and does not pick it up again, and later somebody else will take it home by accident.

bsm_350.text: Across the room, Deacon Vox is accepting Best Performance, and he has prepared nothing, and it does not matter.

bsm_351.text: Deacon Vox says, "I don’t... okay. Two years ago I washed plates at the Meridian and a man came out to the lot and told me I had something."

bsm_352.text: Deacon Vox says, "And everybody in this room has been told their whole life that what they’ve got is the wrong thing to have. That it’s a joke, or it’s dirty, or it’s an accident."

bsm_907.text: Auggie Prine says, "I found a boy in a lot and I told him the thing about him that everybody had been whispering, and I said it kindly, and I meant it kindly, and I have watched what saying it kindly did."

bsm_909.text: Auggie Prine says, "You were nineteen and you were holding a crate."

bsm_91.text: Denny Faust says, "It’s a job that pays in hard credits."

bsm_910.text: Deacon Vox says, "I said YES, Auggie. I have said yes every single day since. You do not get to take that off me as well. It’s the only thing in the whole five years I actually did."

bsm_911.text: Auggie Prine looks at him for a long moment, and then does something he has not done in the entire picture, which is agree.

bsm_914.text: Auggie Prine says, "Alright. You said yes. It’s yours. All of it, the whole five years, the good and the rest. It’s yours and you did it."

bsm_915.text: They sit in the pool. Somewhere in the house a door goes and Kestrel comes out onto the deck with a broken headset around her neck that she has never replaced.

bsm_92.text: Joanie Faust says, "Do you think I’m stupid? Do you think I have lived in this house with you for nineteen years and I am STUPID?"

bsm_921.text: She sits down on the edge of the pool with her feet over the side, and that is all, and it is enough, because these people have never once been able to say the thing.

bsm_922.text: Auggie Prine says, "I want to shoot something."

bsm_923.text: Deacon Vox says, "There’s no licence, Auggie. There’s no mast."

bsm_924.text: Auggie Prine says, "There is a mast on the ridge that nobody has climbed in fourteen months and there is an inspector in Coldwater who is paid to inspect the Basin, and I have met him, and he is one man with a truck."

bsm_925.text: Kestrel says, "That’s not a plan, that’s a grievance with a map."

bsm_926.text: Auggie Prine says, "It is ninety minutes, is what it is. One story. Same people the whole way through."

bsm_927.text: Deacon Vox says, "Auggie. I can’t promise you I can do it."

bsm_928.text: Auggie Prine says, "I did not ask you to promise me anything. I asked you to stand on a mark in a house you know. That is all I have ever asked anybody in fifteen years."

bsm_929.text: Deacon Vox says, "And if it doesn’t happen?"

bsm_930.text: Auggie Prine says, "Then it doesn’t happen, and we go again after lunch, and nobody in this house says a word about it. Nobody in this house has ever said a word about it."

bsm_931.text: Deacon Vox puts his head back against a concrete wall in a drained swimming pool and laughs, once, badly, because his ribs are still wrong.

bsm_933.text: THE PRINE HOUSE, THE LOUNGE SET

bsm_934.text: The lamps go on one at a time. Three of them. It takes a while, because two are broken and Buck Ozarow has to be called.

bsm_935.text: Reed Halloran arrives in a security uniform he does not change out of, and hits his mark, and is home.

bsm_936.text: Scotty Kell comes off a haul route with a boom pole in the cab of a truck that does not belong to him, and nobody asks.

bsm_937.text: Marguerite Sable puts a light where a light should be. Kestrel stands where a camera should be and finds she can see the whole room from there.

bsm_939.text: The house goes quiet, the way it used to, the way rooms do when they have agreed to take something seriously.

bsm_94.text: Joanie Faust says, "I do the washing, Denny. I have done the washing since you were four years old. There is not one thing about you I have not known for years and had the decency to say nothing about."

bsm_941.text: There is no sound man. Auggie Prine says "speed" to nobody, because that is the word, and the word is the job, and the job is what is left.

bsm_946.text: The very last shot of the picture is not the set. The picture cuts backwards, three minutes, to a man alone in a room with a mirror.

bsm_947.text: Deacon Vox, twenty-five, in the room he lived in at nineteen, in front of the same full-length mirror, on the night it matters.

bsm_948.text: He is not warming up. There is nothing to warm up. He is doing the thing he has done in front of this mirror ten thousand times and has not been able to do for a year.

bsm_95.text: The kitchen is very small and there is nowhere in it to stand that is far enough away.

bsm_950.text: The film, which has spent two and a half hours pointing the camera at everybody else’s face: at Auggie in the lot, at the crew at the back of the room, at eleven people looking at the ceiling, finally, in its last thirty seconds, looks.

bsm_951.text: And there it is. The one card. The accident in the womb. The reason for the house, the name, the money, the awards, the mother, the alley, all of it.

bsm_952.text: It is not a punchline and the film does not play it as one. It is just true, the way it has always been true, and it has cost him everything he had.

bsm_953.text: Deacon Vox looks at himself in the mirror for a long moment.

bsm_955.text: Deacon Vox says, "Alright. Okay. There you are."

bsm_956.text: He closes the robe. He puts his hands on the dresser and breathes for a second like a man about to lift something.

bsm_957.text: And then he says the name, the one Kestrel gave him at a kitchen table when he was nineteen and everybody said it out loud until it stuck.

bsm_959.text: He goes downstairs, where three lamps are on and a man with no sound crew is saying "speed" to nobody, because that is the word, and the word is the job, and the job is what is left.
